Up from the Cape daily.How to make it2 shallots, finely diced80ml red wine vinegar1 tsp cracked black pepper24 freshly shucked oysters1kg crushed ice2 lemons, cut into wedgesMix the shallots, vinegar and plenty of cracked pepper. Rest to let the flavours settle.Shuck the oysters, keeping the liquor in the shell.Lay the oysters on crushed ice with lemon wedges and the mignonette in a small bowl with a spoon.Fish and chipsCod in a cold lager batter, thick potatoes done twice. Tartar sauce and lemon.Served in a paper cone at the oyster bar.How to make it150g plain flour50g cornflour300ml cold lager600g potatoes500g flathead fillets, cut in strips2 L vegetable oil for frying100g tartare sauce1 lemon, cut into wedgesWhisk the flour, cornflour and lager to a batter.Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry them.Fry the chips in the oil twice, first at a lower heat, then hot to crisp.Dip the flathead strips in batter and fry in the oil at 180°C until golden.Serve in paper cones with tartare and lemon.MainsWhole boiled lobsterAbout 1¾ lb from our tank, split, brushed with garlic butter and finished under the grill. Drawn butter and lemon.Most guests leave the shell.How to make it2 raw lobsters, about 800g each200g butter3 garlic cloves, crushed2 lemons, cut into wedgesBoil the lobsters in salted water, allowing about 8 minutes per 500g of weight.Melt half the butter with the garlic. Keep the rest for drawn butter.Split the lobsters lengthways and crack the claws. Brush the flesh with the garlic butter.Grill flesh-side up until hot and lightly golden.Serve with drawn butter and lemon.SweetsBlue sea gelatinCoconut cream set firm under a clear sea-blue layer, gummy fish on top.From the main room dessert cart.How to make it6 gelatine leaves400ml coconut milk, warm120g caster sugar10 dried butterfly pea flowers400ml hot water1 bag gummy fishBloom 3 gelatine leaves in cold water and stir into the warm coconut milk with half the sugar.Pour into four glasses and chill until set.Steep the pea flowers in the hot water with the remaining sugar, strain, and stir in 3 bloomed gelatine leaves.Cool to room temperature, then pour over the set coconut layer.Chill until firm, then top with gummy fish.DrinksBlue lagoonVodka and blue curaçao over ice, topped with lemon-lime soda and a lemon wheel.Must be 19 to order.How to make it120ml vodka80ml blue curaçao600ml lemonade1 lemon, cut into wheels1 bag iceFill four tall glasses with ice.Add vodka and blue curaçao to each.Top with lemonade, stir gently and garnish with a lemon wheel.
